questions.question: What is IN's favourite fika (like kanelbullar, dammsugare etc.)?
questions.hint: The classic won clearly - the 'chokladbollar' could not keep up.
questions.solution: Kanelbullar (1st with 54%, in front of chokladbollar with 23%)

questions.question: What is IN's second favourite game?
questions.hint: Blood on the Clocktower won with 39% - this classic card game came second with 31%.

questions.question: What is IN's favourite soft drink?
questions.hint: It even beat water.
questions.solution: Ice tea (30 votes), in front of water (23) and both Sprite and Coca-Cola (15% each)

questions.question: What is IN's least favourite pet?
questions.hint: Almost nobody picked it as their favourite pet.
questions.solution: Hamster (only 8 picked it as a favourite pet - fewer than Dog (38) and Cat (54))

questions.question: How many people answered rap as their favourite genre?
questions.hint: The top 3 genres were pop, indie and rock.

questions.question: How many letters would you need to write the whole periodic table (the symbols of the elements)?
questions.hint: 14 elements have one-letter symbols, the other 104 have two.

questions.question: How many passenger windows does an Airbus A380 (the largest passenger plane) have?
questions.hint: That works out to only 0.4 windows per passenger.

questions.question: How many iPhones were sold in 2025?
questions.hint: That many of them stacked would be equivalent to a dollar-bill stack 27 km high.

questions.question: How many water molecules are there in 1 litre of water?
questions.hint: Water has a molar mass of 18 g/mol and 1 mol = 6.02×10²³ molecules.

questions.question: How often does Little Italy fit into the country Italy?
questions.hint: Italy covers 301,340 km²; Little Italy in Manhattan is 0.05 km².

questions.question: Who is this film director?
questions.hint: A near-fatal car accident at 18 ended his racing dreams and pushed him toward film school.

questions.question: What country is this monument from?
questions.hint: The Incas built it without mortar - the stones fit so tightly you cannot slide a knife between them.

questions.question: Who painted this painting?
questions.hint: One version was stolen from an Oslo museum in 1994, on the opening day of the Winter Olympics.

questions.question: What is this waterfall?
questions.hint: Locally it is called Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders', for its spray visible from kilometres away.

questions.question: What country is this?
questions.hint: The U.S. bought these islands from Denmark in 1917 for $25 million in gold.
questions.solution: The United States (the flag of the U.S. Virgin Islands)

questions.question: Which is the largest organ in the human body?
questions.hint: An organ is two or more tissue types cooperating to carry out specific jobs.

questions.question: Which country has the most time zones (including overseas territories)?
questions.hint: Without overseas territories, Russia would lead with 11.

questions.question: What is the only letter that does not appear in any US state name?
questions.hint: J, Z and X are also rare - but they do appear (New Jersey, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas).

questions.question: What is the only mammal capable of true flight?
questions.hint: Flying squirrels, sugar gliders and colugos do not count - they cannot flap their wings.

questions.question: What is the national animal of Scotland?
questions.hint: It has been the national animal for centuries and symbolises purity, strength and independence.

questions.question: What food never goes rotten?
questions.hint: The first traces of it found are 9,000 years old.

questions.question: What set of equations is written on a plate in the Tekniska Högskolan subway station?
questions.hint: They describe electromagnetism - look on the wall on the side for the subway towards Fruängen.

questions.question: When was Minecraft officially fully released?
questions.hint: The 'Adventure Update' took it out of beta.

questions.question: What is hexakosioihexekontahexaphobia?
questions.hint: From ancient Greek: hexakósioi (six hundred), hexékonta (sixty), héx (six) and phóbos (fear).
questions.solution: The fear of the number 666 (the Number of the Beast)

questions.question: Which country has the most pyramids?
questions.hint: Not Egypt - look further south along the Nile.
questions.solution: Sudan (250-255, vs. Egypt's 118-138; some Sudanese pyramids are far more ancient)
